levels.title: Opioid LASA Pair Recognition
levels.description: Recognize look-alike and sound-alike counterparts among high-potency synthetic opioids.
levels.learningObjective: Identify documented ISMP confusable opioid counterparts.

questions.prompt: Which synthetic opioid is an ISMP-documented look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to fentanyl?
questions.explanation: fentanyl and ALfentanil share similar root letters but possess vastly different pharmacokinetic profiles.

questions.prompt: Which natural opiate is frequently confused with HYDROmorphone due to shared root names?
questions.explanation: HYDROmorphone is approximately 4-7 times more potent than morphine, making mix-ups extremely hazardous.

questions.prompt: Which opioid pairs with ALfentanil on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: ALfentanil and SUFentanil are potent synthetic opioids that look and sound alike.

levels.title: Opioid Tall Man Lettering
levels.description: Distinguish synthetic opioid prefixes and suffixes using ISMP Tall Man standards.
levels.learningObjective: Differentiate fentaNYL, ALfentanil, and HYDROmorphone using correct capitalization.

activities.learningObjective: Construct and identify correct Tall Man lettering for high-alert opioids.

questions.prompt: Convert this opioid name to Tall Man lettering by entering the letters that should be capitalized:
questions.explanation: fentaNYL capitalizes NYL to contrast with the AL prefix of ALfentanil.

questions.prompt: Convert this opioid name to Tall Man lettering by entering the letters that should be capitalized:
questions.explanation: ALfentanil capitalizes AL to distinguish it from fentaNYL and SUFentanil.

questions.prompt: Convert this opioid name to Tall Man lettering by entering the letters that should be capitalized:
questions.explanation: HYDROmorphone capitalizes HYDRO to prevent confusion with morphine.

levels.title: Opioid Memorization & Discrimination
levels.description: Reinforce discrimination across all synthetic opioid prefixes and suffixes.
levels.learningObjective: Accurately recall and discriminate look-alike opioid pairs and Tall Man distinctions.

activities.learningObjective: Discriminate look-alike opioid names and Tall Man letter representations.

questions.prompt: Which drug is the look-alike counterpart to HYDROmorphone differing in the MOR/HYDRO syllables?
questions.explanation: HYDROmorphone and oxyMORphone differ in their prefix and middle syllables and both represent high-potency opioids.

questions.prompt: Which representation correctly applies ISMP Tall Man lettering to fentanyl?
questions.explanation: fentaNYL capitalizes NYL to distinguish it from ALfentanil.

questions.prompt: Which representation correctly applies ISMP Tall Man lettering to sufentanil?
questions.explanation: SUFentanil capitalizes SUF to distinguish it from ALfentanil and fentaNYL.

levels.title: Unit 4 Mastery
levels.description: Comprehensive review of Section 2 opioid pairs followed by an unassisted Tall Man capstone task.
levels.learningObjective: Demonstrate complete unit mastery of high-alert opioid recognition and unassisted Tall Man lettering.

questions.prompt: Which drug is the confusable look-alike counterpart to HYDROmorphone?
questions.explanation: morphine and HYDROmorphone are critical look-alike counterparts on the ISMP high-alert list.

questions.prompt: Which medication is paired with fentaNYL on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: fentaNYL and ALfentanil are paired on the ISMP list due to confusable generic roots.

activities.learningObjective: Independently construct the exact Tall Man lettering for hydromorphone without scaffolding.
